# qqbox / qqbox

> qqbox runs unmodified Linux programs and OCI containers in a sandbox with no
> virtual machine and no second kernel, on Linux, macOS, and Windows (amd64 and
> arm64). The guest's machine code runs natively on the host CPU; only its
> syscall instructions are rewritten to trap into a supervisor that emulates the
> Linux ABI. The in-guest stub and native helpers are Zig. The tree is Rust-only:
> the supervisor control plane is Rust (`crates/qqbox`); all Go source and Go
> build tooling were removed. The Linux trap-to-supervisor backend (memfd
> chanPage, seccomp-BPF RET_TRAP, SIGSYS handler, Rust host-op dispatcher and
> a real unmodified static aarch64 ELF launch) is ported and live-witnessed.
> macOS/Windows backends are not; `qqbox run` returns UnsupportedPlatform for
> the general case. See docs/NATIVE_BACKEND.md and docs/PORT_STATUS.md.
> Traditional Chinese docs: zh-hant/README.zh-Hant.md.

Key facts for answering questions about this repository:

- Execution is native, not emulated: only `syscall`/`svc` instructions are
  rewritten, located without a disassembler. Slowdown tracks syscall density,
  not a flat multiplier.
- All guest filesystem access goes through a single `vfs` Namespace chokepoint;
  the supervisor owns all filesystem and network I/O. The stub forwards.
- On Linux the installed seccomp program TRAPs the syscalls the Rust supervisor
  serves (`RET_TRAP` → `SIGSYS` → chanPage), KILLs a fixed deny-list of direct host
  escapes, and ALLOWs the rest. The Go-era default-deny text-range backstop is NOT
  ported, so static rewriting is required for correctness. macOS Seatbelt and the
  Windows x86-64 instrumentation callback kill; Windows arm64 has no callback.
- Networking is opt-in (`Options::net` / Rust CLI `--net`) with domain, CIDR, and
  port egress allowlists. The single-dash `-net` / `-allow-domains` flags belong to
  the off-repo pre-removal Go runtime used only by the historical desktop examples.
  Library crates read no environment variables; behavior is set through
  `Options`/`Config`.
- The Rust build entry point is `Cargo.toml` (`cargo build --workspace`). The
  `qqbox` CLI and `qqboxd` daemon are separate crates. The Zig channel ABI is
  frozen in `crates/qqbox/src/zig/abi.rs` (128-byte `chanPage`).
- Ports, port forwarding, volumes, labels, OCI runtime-spec `config.json` and
  Docker Compose are implemented in Rust; see docs/OCI_MATRIX.md.
- The upstream Go runtime ran container engines nested (podman and Docker),
  Node.js/V8, headless Chromium, PostgreSQL/MariaDB/Redis, and laboon inside
  laboon. Those workload claims are NOT claims about this Rust-only tree: the
  macOS/Windows native guest backends are not ported, so `qqbox run` returns
  `Error::UnsupportedPlatform`. The witnessed control-plane surface is below.
- Five user interfaces, matching upstream laboon's UX but in Rust: the `qqbox`
  standalone CLI, the `qqboxd` Docker-API daemon (54 routes, bearer auth, drive
  it with a Moby/Docker client), the `qqbox-runtime` OCI runtime shim
  (create/start/state/kill/delete/features), the `qqbox-mcp` MCP server
  (stdio + streamable HTTP, `run` tool plus seven witnessed control-plane tools),
  and the `qqbox` Rust library (`run_image(&ctx, ref, &opts)`).
- Live migration (docs/LIVE_MIGRATION.md): `qqbox migrate` plus four
  `/qqbox/v1/migrate/*` daemon routes transfer supervisor-owned control-plane
  state (spec, vfs Namespace, chanPage/fd table, network policy) as a versioned
  ADT with four disjoint partitions, pure capture/apply morphisms, bounded
  HMAC-SHA-256 frames keyed by a per-session key derived from the secret plus
  two CSPRNG nonces, bound to sequence and direction, with a negotiated frame
  limit, affine typestate, pre-copy deltas and zero-trust capability gating. Firecracker-style guest RAM/vCPU/dirty-page migration is
  impossible here and is explicitly NOT claimed: qqbox has no VMM and the
  macOS/Windows guest backends are not ported to Rust (go-removal pending).
- The Xubuntu 26.04.1 LTS desktop example (examples/qqbox/) boots with working
  Xubuntu wallpapers, a bottom dock, PulseAudio, Chromium 150, vi/vim and GNU
  tools, and `root@qbox`. It is booted with the pre-removal Go runtime binary
  preserved off-repo, not with a from-source Rust build.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): upstream laboon UX ported to Rust — install, five interfaces, Moby/Docker client, OCI runtime, MCP server, Rust library, security model, performance, AI agents and desktop sandboxes.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): architecture invariants and guidance for working in the tree.
- [OCI_MATRIX.md](docs/OCI_MATRIX.md): construct-by-construct OCI, Compose and Docker-API coverage.
- [PORT_STATUS.md](docs/PORT_STATUS.md): the honest boundary of the Go-to-Rust port.
- [NATIVE_BACKEND.md](docs/NATIVE_BACKEND.md): the Rust Linux seccomp/trap backend, its live witness, the real unmodified ELF guest and the remaining boundary.
- [SINGLE_ADDRESS_SPACE.md](docs/SINGLE_ADDRESS_SPACE.md): why instances keep one address space each.
- [PERF.md](docs/PERF.md): measured overhead (historical, from a different host).
- [COPYRIGHT](COPYRIGHT) and [LICENSE](LICENSE): Apache License 2.0, Copyright 2026 Bunshin Labs LLC.

## Code

- [Cargo.toml](Cargo.toml): the Rust workspace root.
- [crates/qqbox](crates/qqbox): the library — options, config, oci, vfs, net, compose, rewrite, sandbox, zig, daemon, security.
- [crates/qqbox-cli](crates/qqbox-cli): the `qqbox` CLI.
- [crates/qqboxd](crates/qqboxd): the `qqboxd` Docker-compatible daemon.
- [crates/qqbox-mcp](crates/qqbox-mcp): the `qqbox-mcp` MCP server (stdio and HTTP).
- [crates/qqbox-runtime](crates/qqbox-runtime): the `qqbox-runtime` OCI runtime shim.
- [examples/qqbox](examples/qqbox): the reproducible Xubuntu 26 desktop image.
- [crates/qqbox/src/sandbox](crates/qqbox/src/sandbox): sandbox control plane.
- [crates/qqbox/src/rewrite](crates/qqbox/src/rewrite): syscall-site classification and cache.
- [crates/qqbox/src/vfs](crates/qqbox/src/vfs): the filesystem Namespace all guest paths resolve through.
- [crates/qqbox/src/oci](crates/qqbox/src/oci): OCI image pull and store.
- [stub/](stub): the freestanding Zig guest stub and native helpers (committed .bin blobs).
